question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

$\frac{2}{5}\int_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\sqrt{{log}_{2}\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡2$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\log_{2}\left(\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\right).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\,⟹\,\ln{\left(2 \right)}\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $32$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $5$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}\int_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\sqrt{{log}_{2}\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\int_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{2}\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)}}\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\int_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}2\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}{5}\int_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left(\operatorname{ln}2\cdot 2\sqrt{u}\right)|_{2}^{5} \\ & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot\left((2\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{2})\operatorname{ln}2\right)\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: positive x interval; original real logarithm branch; sqrt log>=0, denominator log nonzero in interior; q-31643 convergent improper lower endpoint
